---
title: "In Quarto"
subtitle: "Figures for books, papers and websites"
---

prism was built with books in mind as much as agents. Diagrams are SVG, so they
stay sharp at any size, keep their text selectable and searchable, and diff
sensibly in git.

## The short version

prism results render themselves in any IPython-compatible environment, which
includes Quarto's Jupyter engine. Return the object from a code cell:

````markdown
```{{python}}
#| label: fig-pipeline
#| fig-cap: "The ingestion pipeline"
#| echo: false
import prism
prism.diagram("pipeline.yaml")
```
````

`prism.diagram()` returns an object with a `_repr_svg_`, so Quarto embeds the
SVG inline — no intermediate file, no rasterisation.

## Writing the spec inline

For a one-off figure it is often clearest to keep the spec in the document:

````markdown
```{{python}}
#| echo: false
import prism
prism.diagram("""
type: cycle
title: Build-measure-learn
center: {label: Kaizen}
steps:
  - {label: Build, icon: hammer, accent: 0}
  - {label: Measure, icon: gauge, accent: 1}
  - {label: Learn, icon: lightbulb, accent: 2}
""")
```
````

## Matching the document's theme

Point `theme:` at a YAML file next to your manuscript and every figure in the
book picks up the same palette and typography:

```yaml
type: flow
theme: ../theme/house.yaml
steps:
  - {label: Draft}
  - {label: Review}
  - {label: Ship}
```

The bundled `paper` theme is a reasonable starting point for print: serif
typography, warm surface, square corners, hairline strokes.

## Rendering to PDF

Quarto's Typst and LaTeX paths both accept SVG figures. Because prism paints
its own surface colour, a figure keeps its intended background rather than
inheriting the page.

One caveat worth stating plainly: prism measures text against the metrics of
Arial, Times New Roman and Courier New. Those have metric-compatible clones
almost everywhere (Helvetica on macOS; Liberation or Croscore on Linux), so
boxes fit. If you override `typography.family` with a font prism has not
measured, expect looser boxes — see [Themes](themes.qmd).

## Batch rendering

For a manuscript with many figures, render them all ahead of the build:

```bash
for spec in figures/*.yaml; do
  prism render "$spec" -o "figures/$(basename "${spec%.yaml}").svg"
done
```

The same approach builds this site's gallery — see
`scripts/build_gallery.py` in the repository, which renders every bundled
example in every bundled theme and generates the [Catalog](catalog.qmd) and
[Themes](themes.qmd) pages from the result. Documentation that is generated
from the examples cannot drift from them.
